attempts.raw_response: From there, tap the Add Friends button, then choose By Snapcode. Your camera roll will open, allowing you to select the photo containing the snapcode. Snapchat will scan the image and automatically recognize the code, adding the friend if it's valid. You can also find snapcodes on other people's phones or printed materials—just take a clear photo of the code and follow the same steps. This method is especially handy for adding friends quickly without needing to search for usernames. Remember, the snapcode must be unobstructed and well-lit for the app to read it correctly. Once added, you can start snapping right away.

pair.human_continuation: It's toward the bottom of the profile page screen. This is a small tab on the top right side of the screen.  You won't be able to add contacts from your address book if Snapchat doesn't have access to your contacts. If you haven't added your phone number to your Snapchat account yet, do so when prompted. Contacts are usually listed in alphabetical order. Type your contact's name into the Search bar at the top of the screen to speed up your search. You can add any contact with an + Add next to their name.  You won't see the names of contacts whom you've already added in Snapchat here. If the contact doesn't have a Snapchat account, you'll see Invite to the right of their name.
pair.prefix:
You can also add a friend by snapcode from a picture in your camera roll by tapping Add Friends on the profile page, tapping By Snapcode, and selecting a photo with the snapcode.
The Snapchat app icon is a white ghost with a yellow background. If you aren't already logged into Snapchat, tap Log In and enter your username (or email address) and password. Doing so will open your profile page.
